rationale: All four lenses ran and parsed cleanly against an existing spec, and every candidate finding was verified against source within budget. 9 findings survive triage (4 critical, 5 major) — most notably the spec's required modelSource-based override protection was never implemented, the version-ranking regex can't score undated Claude model ids, and the new auto-resolver loop still forces catalog models onto anthropic-subscription while separately leaking a stale CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL. 5 findings were dismissed as verified non-issues and 0 were deferred; see code-review-brief.md for the full list.

findings.title: Version regex can't rank undated model ids
findings.problem: extractVersionParts's genMatch regex (`claude(?:[-_.]?(\d+))?(?:[-_.](\d+))?`) assumes version digits immediately follow the literal `claude` prefix, but every real Claude model id shown elsewhere in this diff (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) has the tier word between `claude` and the digits, so the optional digit groups never match and genMatch[1]/genMatch[2] are always undefined -> generation score is always [0,0].
findings.impact: Ranking between two non-dated versions of the same tier (e.g. claude-opus-4-6 vs claude-opus-4-7) collapses to compareRankedModels' alphabetical id tie-break, which does not correlate with recency (and actively misorders multi-digit versions, e.g. '4-10' sorting before '4-9') — undermining the 'always resolve to the current model' goal for the common undated naming pattern this diff's own examples use.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the generation regex to skip an optional tier word between `claude` and the digits, e.g. match `claude(?:-(?:sonnet|opus|haiku))?[-_.]?(\d+)(?:[-_.](\d+))?`, and add a case covering `claude-sonnet-4-6`-style ids to catch a regression.

findings.title: Malformed catalog entry aborts entire tier ranking
findings.problem: rankModel throws ConfigurationError when getModelId(model) is falsy (all of deployment_name/base_name/label empty), but isClaudeCompatibleModel doesn't require an id — it can pass an entry via the `provider` field alone. The ranking pipeline (`catalog.filter(isClaudeCompatibleModel).map(rankModel).sort(...)`) is not wrapped in a try/catch, so .map() throws synchronously for the whole tier.
findings.impact: One catalog entry with empty id fields (valid per the LlmModel type since the fields are required strings but empty string is falsy) but a matching provider name aborts ranking for every other otherwise-valid candidate in that tier; the outer per-tier catch in claude.plugin.ts swallows it and the tier silently keeps its old configured model (or throws ConfigurationError if unconfigured), instead of ranking around the one bad entry.
findings.recommendation: Guard the map step, e.g. `.map(m => { try { return rankModel(m); } catch { return null; } }).filter((r): r is RankedClaudeModel => r !== null)`, so one malformed entry is skipped rather than aborting the tier.

findings.title: Haiku tier has no static fallback model
findings.problem: staticFallback('haiku') searches ClaudePluginMetadata.recommendedModels (`['claude-sonnet-4-6', 'claude-4-opus', 'gpt-4.1']`, claude.plugin.ts:97) for an id matching /haiku/i, but none of the three entries contain 'haiku'.
findings.impact: On a catalog fetch failure (network/auth error) with no currently configured haiku model — e.g. a first-ever run with no network — resolveClaudeModel('haiku') always throws ConfigurationError instead of falling back to a static default, unlike the sonnet and opus tiers which do have matching fallback entries.
findings.recommendation: Add a haiku-matching id to ClaudePluginMetadata.recommendedModels (e.g. 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001') so staticFallback('haiku') can resolve.

findings.title: Explicit-override check ignores modelSource
findings.problem: The spec's Design 2 requires reusing the existing modelSource/CODEMIE_MODEL_SOURCE convention (resolve live only when a tier's modelSource is 'default', or when the current model is stale/retired) mirroring resolveCopilotModel's assertExplicitCopilotModelAllowed gate. resolveClaudeModel never reads env.CODEMIE_MODEL_SOURCE or any modelSource value at all — it substitutes a presence-in-catalog check (`currentModel && availableModels.includes(currentModel)`) that treats any non-empty CODEMIE_*_MODEL as explicit.
findings.impact: ConfigLoader.exportProviderEnvVars unconditionally sets CODEMIE_MODEL/CODEMIE_HAIKU_MODEL/CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL/CODEMIE_OPUS_MODEL from config.* before any provider overlay (src/utils/config.ts:1418-1425), so a stale-but-still-catalog-present default value the user never explicitly chose is treated as explicit and never re-ranked against newer catalog entries — the required design behavior for the common 'default, never explicitly set' case never runs.
findings.recommendation: Read env.CODEMIE_MODEL_SOURCE for the tier and gate the live-resolution path on it being 'default' (or the current model being absent from the catalog), matching resolveCopilotModel's gate in copilot-cli.models.ts:213-217.

findings.title: No test covers explicit-override protection
findings.problem: No test in the repo exercises resolveClaudeModel's 'leave a still-valid configured model untouched' check (`if (currentModel && availableModels.includes(currentModel)) return null;`) against a non-empty live catalog — no claude.models.test.ts exists, and the two test files that execute the beforeRun hook containing this loop never set CODEMIE_JWT_TOKEN/CODEMIE_BASE_URL/CODEMIE_URL, so fetchCatalog always takes the empty-catalog fallback branch.
findings.impact: A regression that always overwrites the configured model (or picks the wrong ranked candidate) would silently replace a user's explicitly configured, still-valid Claude model on every `codemie claude` run, and no test in the repo would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add src/agents/plugins/claude/__tests__/claude.models.test.ts covering per-tier ranking, fetch-failure fallback, and explicit-override-respect against a populated catalog, per the spec's own Testing section.

findings.title: Auto-resolver loop not scoped away from anthropic-subscription
findings.problem: The new per-tier auto-resolve loop in ClaudePlugin's beforeRun runs unconditionally for every provider, including anthropic-subscription — the provider this diff's Design 4 explicitly says has 'no CodeMie catalog to resolve a model from' and should defer entirely to the claude CLI's own defaults. When config.codeMieUrl is also set for anthropic-subscription (a combination the provider template itself supports, anthropic-subscription.template.ts:117-120), fetchCatalog takes the SSO credential path and can successfully resolve a real CodeMie-catalog model.
findings.impact: That resolved model is then written into ANTHROPIC_MODEL/ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL/CODEMIE_MODEL, directly re-introducing the 'forced model onto the claude CLI' behavior Goal 3 and Design 4 set out to remove. When codeMieUrl is unset instead, the same loop throws a ConfigurationError per tier (no catalog, no current model) that is caught and logged at logger.warn on every single anthropic-subscription run — functionally harmless but spurious warning noise the spec did not intend.
findings.recommendation: Scope the auto-resolve loop (or resolveClaudeModel/fetchCatalog itself) to skip entirely when the active provider is anthropic-subscription, so that path always defers to the claude CLI's built-in defaults as designed.

findings.title: Native Anthropic env vars overwritten without a check
findings.problem: The auto-resolve loop writes resolution.selectedModel to both the generic CODEMIE_*_MODEL var and every native var in TIER_TARGET_VARS[tier].native (ANTHROPIC_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL) whenever resolution is non-null. resolveClaudeModel's own 'don't override an explicit choice' check only inspects the generic CODEMIE_*_MODEL var (claude.models.ts:306) — it never checks whether the native var itself was already set.
findings.impact: A user who sets a native var directly (a mechanism the claude CLI itself supports) without also setting the matching CODEMIE_*_MODEL is silently overwritten by the auto-resolved model on every run, contradicting the spec's Goal 2 ('a user's explicit model choice ... env var ... is never silently overridden').
findings.recommendation: Before writing a native var, check whether it was already explicitly set (e.g. `if (!env[nativeVar]) env[nativeVar] = resolution.selectedModel;`), or fold native-var presence into resolveClaudeModel's own override check.

findings.title: Existing tests assert removed model-alias behavior
findings.problem: exportEnvVars now unconditionally blanks CODEMIE_MODEL/CODEMIE_HAIKU_MODEL/CODEMIE_OPUS_MODEL to '', but three pre-existing tests (lines 179-209) still assert the removed alias-normalization values (e.g. `expect(env.CODEMIE_MODEL).toBe('claude-haiku-4-5-20251001')`) or toBeUndefined(), and a fourth test in src/agents/core/__tests__/model-tier-config.test.ts:268-290 asserts env.CODEMIE_MODEL equals a specific model id via the same ConfigLoader path.
findings.impact: None of these tests were updated in this diff; they will fail against the new blanking behavior (actual value is '' in every case), breaking the normal CI/pre-commit test run for this branch.
findings.recommendation: Update the affected assertions in both files to match the new always-blank behavior before merge (subject to the repo's explicit-request testing policy).

findings.title: CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL not blanked like the other tiers
findings.problem: exportEnvVars blanks env.CODEMIE_MODEL, env.CODEMIE_HAIKU_MODEL, and env.CODEMIE_OPUS_MODEL to '' but never mentions or blanks env.CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL — the tier newly wired into the auto-update loop in the same diff. ConfigLoader.exportProviderEnvVars (src/utils/config.ts:1424) unconditionally sets env.CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL = config.sonnetModel ?? '' before this provider overlay runs, exactly like the other three tiers, and BaseAgentAdapter.transformEnvVars projects a truthy CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL straight into ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL before beforeRun even runs.
findings.impact: Any anthropic-subscription profile with a previously saved sonnet model leaks that stale value into ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL/CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL on every run, directly contradicting Design 4's stated goal that this provider path lets the claude CLI's own defaults take over for all tiers.
findings.recommendation: Add `env.CODEMIE_SONNET_MODEL = '';` alongside the other three blanked vars in exportEnvVars.
